original_question: Let Omega be a simply connected bounded open subset of R^2 with smooth boundary, and consider the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem Delta u + lambda u = 0 in Omega with u = 0 on ∂Omega. Must the nodal line of every second eigenfunction be a simple open curve whose endpoints are two distinct points of ∂Omega?
target_in_paper: Problem 6.2 in Section 6, "Payne’s nodal line conjecture".
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper’s actual target almost exactly: it uses the planar Dirichlet Laplacian, assumes a bounded simply connected domain with smooth boundary, focuses on second eigenfunctions, and asks for the stronger open conclusion stated in the paper—namely that the nodal line should be a simple open curve meeting the boundary at two distinct points, rather than only Payne’s original weaker claim that the nodal line is not closed.
missing_details: The paper’s surrounding setup first fixes the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem on a bounded connected open set Ω ⊂ R^n, n ≥ 2, and then specializes to n = 2 in the nodal-line discussion.
A "second eigenfunction" should be identified precisely as any eigenfunction associated with the second Dirichlet eigenvalue λ2; this matters if λ2 has multiplicity greater than 1.
The nodal line is explicitly the interior zero set {x ∈ Ω : u2(x) = 0}.

To make "simple open curve whose endpoints are two distinct points of ∂Ω" fully stand-alone, it is best to say that the nodal set is a simple curve in Ω whose closure in Ω̄ is homeomorphic to a closed interval and meets ∂Ω exactly at two distinct endpoints.
The nearby context distinguishes this stronger problem from Payne’s original conjecture, which only says the nodal line is not a closed curve.

The paper also notes that this phenomenon fails for non-simply-connected domains and can fail if the operator is changed from Δ to Δ - q with variable coefficient q, so the question should stay exactly with the Laplacian and the simply connected hypothesis.
refined_question: Let Ω ⊂ R^2 be a bounded simply connected domain with smooth boundary, and let u2 be any eigenfunction corresponding to the second eigenvalue λ2 of the Dirichlet Laplacian, i.e. Δu2 + λ2 u2 = 0 in Ω and u2 = 0 on ∂Ω. Is the nodal set N(u2) := {x ∈ Ω : u2(x) = 0} necessarily a simple open curve in Ω whose closure in Ω̄ meets ∂Ω at exactly two distinct points?
justification: Section 6 introduces the Dirichlet eigenvalue problem (equation (7)) on a bounded connected open set Ω ⊂ R^n and recalls that a second eigenfunction has exactly two nodal domains by Courant’s theorem (Section 6, introductory discussion, PDF pp. 4-5). It then states Payne’s original conjecture as Conjecture 6.1: for n = 2, the nodal line {x ∈ Ω : u2(x) = 0} is not a closed curve (PDF p. 5). Immediately after that, the paper gives the stronger open problem as Problem 6.2: if Ω is simply connected and has smooth boundary, prove that the nodal line of any second eigenfunction is a simple open curve whose endpoints are two distinct points of ∂Ω (PDF p. 5). Your draft matches Problem 6.2, not merely Conjecture 6.1, and only needs minor clarifications of the eigenvalue/eigenfunction indexing and the precise geometric meaning of the nodal line and its endpoints.
